input: Find bribery and corruption cases involving Trafigura

output.assessment: As of 2026-11-10, Trafigura presents elevated bribery and corruption risk, including an admitted Petrobras bribery conspiracy and a Swiss first-instance conviction concerning Angola; the named corporate defendant in those cases was Trafigura Beheer B.V., not the Singapore group holding company itself. The events below concern four underlying matters, with subsequent procedural developments identified as updates rather than separate schemes. The Swiss conviction was appealed, a final Dutch/Jamaica disposition was not verified, and the latest Malta ruling acquitted the local agent’s brothers—not Trafigura—while other prosecutions remained pending as reported in July 2026.

events.summary: MaltaToday reported that Trafigura paid a purported consultancy fee into a Swiss account benefiting Enemalta consultant Frank Sammut, allegedly constituting a bribe connected with oil supplies.
events.parties: Trafigura (precise corporate entity not identified); Frank Sammut; Energy & Environment Consultants Ltd; Enemalta; local agent George Farrugia.
events.status: alleged; this report does not establish a corporate charge or conviction of Trafigura; see the related 2026 update below.

events.summary: Dutch authorities investigated whether Trafigura’s payment to CCOC Association involved bribery and other offences, while the Privy Council upheld the taking of witness evidence in open court in Jamaica without determining bribery guilt.
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer BV Amsterdam; CCOC Association; Jamaican political-party officials sought as witnesses.
events.status: investigated; the 2021 decision concerned evidence-taking, not conviction or acquittal; final criminal disposition not verified.
events.jurisdiction: Netherlands investigation; mutual legal assistance proceedings in Jamaica and appeal to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

events.type: Foreign bribery — FCPA guilty plea concerning Petrobras
events.summary: Trafigura Beheer B.V. pleaded guilty to conspiracy to violate the FCPA’s anti-bribery provisions over payments to Petrobras officials to obtain and retain business during approximately 2003–2014.
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer B.V.; Petrobras officials; intermediaries and other co-conspirators.
events.jurisdiction: United States, Southern District of Florida; underlying conduct concerned Brazil.
events.amount: USD 80,488,040 criminal fine and USD 46,510,257 forfeiture, with credit of up to USD 26,829,346 against the fine for related Brazilian payments (as_of 2024-03-28); the credit means the resolutions should not simply be added together.

events.type: Foreign bribery and corporate organisational failures — Angola
events.summary: The Swiss Federal Criminal Court convicted the Trafigura corporate defendant for organisational deficiencies that enabled bribery of an Angolan public official during 2009–2011.
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer B.V., identified in the prosecutor’s indictment; former senior executive Mike Wainwright; an Angolan public official; an intermediary.
events.status: convicted at first instance; judgment expressly not final as_of 2025-01-31; see the subsequent appeal update below.
events.jurisdiction: Switzerland, Federal Criminal Court; underlying conduct concerned Angola.
events.amount: CHF 3,000,000 corporate fine and USD 145,000,000 compensatory claim against the company, using the court’s stated figures (as_of 2025-01-31).

events.type: Brazilian leniency settlement — same Petrobras scheme as the US case
events.summary: Brazil’s Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office reported approval of Trafigura Beheer’s leniency agreement covering corrupt Petrobras fuel-oil transactions during 2003–2014, with fines and restitution to the Union and Petrobras.
events.parties: Trafigura Beheer; Ministério Público Federal; Brazilian Union; Petrobras.
events.status: settled; leniency agreement homologated, as reported on 2025-07-16.
events.amount: BRL 435 million in fines and restitution (as_of 2025-07-16; rounded figure stated in the MPF release).

events.type: Appeal update — same Swiss Angola bribery case
events.summary: Trafigura appealed the Swiss finding that it lacked sufficient systems to prevent bribery, continuing the Angola proceedings rather than creating a separate bribery case.
events.parties: Trafigura, concerning the corporate defendant in the Angola case.
events.status: convicted at first instance; appealed; no subsequent appeal disposition verified as_of 2026-11-10.

events.type: Related acquittal and pending-prosecution update — same Malta Enemalta matter
events.summary: A Maltese court acquitted George Farrugia’s brothers after finding them victims rather than accomplices in the oil-procurement corruption scheme linked to alleged Trafigura consultancy payments, while principal prosecutions remained pending.
events.parties: Trafigura (precise corporate entity not identified); local agent George Farrugia; Raymond, Antonio (Twanny), Salvu, Emanuel and Gaetano Farrugia; Frank Sammut; Tancred Tabone.
events.status: acquitted: the Farrugia brothers only; other prosecutions remained pending as_of 2026-07-07; this was not a reported acquittal of Trafigura.

missing_fields: events[0].parties and events[6].parties: the precise Trafigura corporate entity involved in the Malta allegations was not identified.
events[0].status and events[6].status: a Trafigura-specific corporate charge or final disposition in Malta was not verified.
events[1].status: final disposition of the Dutch/Jamaica criminal investigation as_of 2026-11-10 was not verified.

events[5].status: a subsequent Swiss appeal disposition as_of 2026-11-10 was not verified.
events[5].amount: no new monetary ruling was stated in the appeal report.
events[6].amount: no monetary amount was quantified for the related acquittal.

citations.title: Trafigura and former executive found guilty of bribing Angolan official | Reuters
excerpts: BELLINZONA, Switzerland, Jan 31 (Reuters) - Switzerland's top criminal court convicted trading house Trafigura and a former senior executive of corruption on Friday in an unprecedented case over payments made to an Angolan official in exchange for oil contracts. It ordered Trafigura to pay a fine of 3 million Swiss francs ($3.3 million) and $145.6 million in compensation, and sentenced Trafigura's former Chief Operating Officer Mike Wainwright
Prosecutors alleged that Trafigura and others paid bribes of over $5 million via a network of intermediaries to the Angolan official to win oil deals from 2009

basis.reasoning: The indictment supplies the corporate defendant’s legal name; the anonymised court release establishes organisational liability, the CHF 3 million fine, USD 145 million corporate claim and non-finality. Reuters links the verdict to Trafigura and Wainwright. The monetary figures follow the primary court release rather than the differing press figure.
